# Pet voice — lessons

The top block is regenerated by `python3 pet_voice.py learn` from every receipt in
`evidence/`. It also writes `learned/voice-scores.json`, which the next `talk`/`relay`
reads: model order (working, fastest first), the accepted TTS request shape per model and
voice×language intelligibility (`--adapt` swaps a voice that listeners keep mis-hearing).
The curated section below is for lessons a script cannot infer — add one line per new lesson.

## Curated lessons

- **Use the MBP Keychain key directly in-process.** `gemini-agent` deliberately refuses
  generation (`status|inventory|probe` only); voice work uses `pet_voice.py`, which reads the
  same Keychain item with `/usr/bin/security` and never prints it. (2026-11-14)
- **Check the live model list, not memory.** `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` returned 404 for this
  project although listed; 3.8 TTS/text models worked. `learn` drops 403/404/per-day-quota
  models from the order automatically. (2026-11-14)
- **Newest is not fastest.** On 14 Nov `gemini-3.8-flash` stalled >2 min on an audio+JSON
  listen request while `gemini-3.5-flash` answered in ~8 s (transcript accuracy 0.98) and
  `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` in ~3 s (same accuracy, but it skipped "address the next pet by
  name"). Calls now time out (45 s listen / 90 s TTS) and fall through to the next model;
  `learn` counts timeouts as failures. (2026-11-14)
- **Background jobs over RDC die with the call.** `cmd &` inside `start_process` was killed;
  run long relays in a named tmux session via the RDC `session.py` helper. (2026-11-14)
- **Two speakers max per Gemini TTS request**, so multi-agent talk is synthesized per turn;
  that also keeps every pet's own voice and makes runs resumable per turn. (2026-11-14)
- **Free-tier TTS runs out mid-relay.** The personal key got ~45 TTS calls/day across the four
  TTS models; then every model returned per-day 429 with RetryInfo ≈10.6 h (reset ≈08:00 UTC).
  `learn` stores `cooldownUntil` per model and the next run starts with the Live API voices,
  which have a separate quota. `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest` recited a Finnish line
  word for word (fidelity 1.0); `gemini-3.8-live` spoke but returned no transcript. (2026-11-14)
- **A Live voice may answer the line instead of reading it.** In the second relay
  `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest` replied to two lines in its own words (script
  fidelity 0.19), so the next listener heard something the speaker never "said". Every Live
  turn now checks `outputAudioTranscription` against the script, re-voices once with a
  stricter frame below 0.8, and `learn` multiplies each TTS model's rank by its mean
  fidelity. (2026-11-14)
- **Any provider error should fall through, not stop the relay.** `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`
  returned 503 "high demand" six times in a row and the relay stopped at turn 26 although
  two other listen models were available. Now every non-400 error moves to the next model;
  the run resumes from the failed turn with the same `--run-id`. (2026-11-14)
- **Older TTS models reject `speech_metadata`** (400 on 3.1-preview and 2.5-preview); the
  style-prefix request works. The accepted shape per model is learned, so later calls skip
  the failing attempt. (2026-11-14)
- **Listeners drift into the language they just heard.** In the first full relay a fi-FI pet
  answered in Danish and hi-IN came back in English (language kept 91 %). Fix: the turn prompt
  now repeats the target language and asks for native script. Second relay: language kept
  91 % → 97 %; the same fi-FI pet now answered Danish in Finnish and hi-IN came back in
  Devanagari. (2026-11-14)
- **A listener can "hear" the wrong language.** Meta (en-US) transcribed MariaDB's Swedish as
  garbled English (accuracy 0.58). That pair is listed as weak; with two such samples
  `--adapt` swaps the speaker's voice. (2026-11-14)
- **Score the voice against what was actually said.** When the Live voice paraphrased, the
  first scoring blamed six English voices. Live turns now carry `ttsSpoken`; voice×language
  clarity compares the listener's transcript with that, and script fidelity is a separate
  TTS-model metric. Open limitation: a listener that transliterates (Devanagari ↔ Latin)
  scores near 0 although it understood — hi-IN 0.52 needs a script-aware check. (2026-11-14)
- **Overwriting a file iCloud is syncing can fail.** Re-finalizing a resumed run raised
  EDEADLK ("Resource deadlock avoided") on the iCloud copy and stopped before `learn`.
  Copies now go through a temp file + `os.replace` with retries, and failures are reported in
  the receipt instead of crashing. (2026-11-15)
- **Measure intelligibility, don't guess it.** The listener only receives audio; comparing
  its transcript with what the speaker meant to say gives a free per-voice, per-language
  quality signal on every turn. (2026-11-14)
